turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Morning, Nate. You got a sec? I need to vent about the cluster migration.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Sure, what's up? I saw the incident report from last week. That was rough.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Rough is an understatement. I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was ready. My fault entirely.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Ouch. So the traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it? I heard it was bad.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, it couldn't handle a single request. And because I flipped the global DNS, the outage lasted for hours and hit every region. Customers in three continents were down.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's brutal. But at least you know what went wrong, right? You waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS this time?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I did. I literally sat there, watched the health check go green, and then switched. Traffic moved over without a hitch. No drama.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. So we're back to normal? No more surprises?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: For now. But I'm not trusting myself again. I'm going to set up health-check-gated DNS failover so traffic auto-routes away from a dead cluster. No more manual waiting.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's smart. Automate the thing you almost got fired for.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly. I'll write it up this afternoon.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey Melanie, quick question. Did you push that feature to the API service yesterday?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Yeah, I did. Why? Something wrong?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I'm seeing a weird 500 error on the /v2/endpoint. It's not in the logs from the test environment.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Oh no. I deployed without running the test suite. I was in a hurry, thought it was a trivial change.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Melanie... you know that's how regressions happen. And guess what? A regression slipped into production. The error is from your change.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Damn. I'm sorry. I'll roll it back right now.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Please do. But also, we need a better process. You can't keep doing this manually.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: You're right. I'm going to set up a CI gate that blocks merges without tests. No exceptions.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's the right call. If the gate is enforced, untested code never reaches production. Period.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: I'll have it in place by end of week. And I'll add a test for that endpoint too.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. I saw you pushed the new DNS failover config. Looks solid.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Thanks. But I need to tell you something — I was wrong about the health-check approach.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: What do you mean? You waited for the health check before switching DNS last time, and it worked fine.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: It worked once. But turns out that wasn't enough. I realized that waiting for the health check manually is still a human step. And humans get distracted, or tired, or overconfident.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: So what did you change?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: We replaced the manual wait with fully automated health-check-gated DNS. The system checks the cluster every 10 seconds, and if it's unhealthy, it automatically routes traffic away. No human can skip the wait because there's no wait — it's continuous.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: That's a big upgrade. So even if you're on vacation, the failover just happens?

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Exactly. And I also added a hard rule: DNS changes are only allowed through the automation. I can't manually override it anymore. That's the part that fell short before — I could always just say 'I'll check it myself' and skip the gate.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Good. So the old approach was insufficient because it relied on you being perfect. Now it's system-enforced.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Right. And combined with the CI gate from last week, we've got both sides covered — code quality and infrastructure resilience. I feel a lot better now.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: You should. This is the kind of thing that prevents the next multi-hour outage.

turns.speaker: Melanie
turns.text: Fingers crossed. But at least if it happens, it'll be because the system failed, not because I forgot to wait.
